title: OpenAI says it used AI to identify suspect who planted listening device in office

image.caption: OpenAI said on Tuesday that the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had arrested one ‌of its employees in connection with a sophisticated listening device found hidden in one of the company's offices. (Dado Ruvic/Illustration/Reuters)

blocks.text: U.S. federal agents arrested a Saudi national employed as an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing ​a hidden audio recording device in an ​executive conference room at the AI company, the U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday.
Tech firm says FBI now investigating and an arrest has been made
OpenAI ​had used its internal AI ​models to identify the individual responsible for planting the device and to trace ​its origins, it said in an ⁠X post.

"At this ⁠time, we ‌have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," ⁠according to the AI company.
The company said it referred the matter to the FBI, which ‌is continuing to investigate. The FBI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for more details.
OpenAI CEO tells world leaders to help guide AI's future
Earlier this year, a Texas man was charged with throwing a Molotov cocktail at the home of OpenAI CEO Sam ​Altman and attempting to set fire to the AI firm's headquarters.

OpenAI faces scrutiny over security incidents ⁠involving its AI systems. Reuters and other media outlets reported recently that the company ⁠had told investors its annualized revenue for September was almost $50 billion US, a drop ⁠from ⁠what it signaled earlier.

blocks.text: OpenAI said on ​Friday it fired three researchers after an investigation found they had violated company policies ​on handling sensitive information.

The ⁠statement came after the researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture that had allowed researchers to raise safety ⁠concerns.
